one_liner: Magento/Adobe Commerce has broad REST and GraphQL APIs, but each merchant store hosts its own instance, so credentials come per-customer via an integration (OAuth 1.0a) or IMS on the cloud service.
auth_notes: Third-party integrations use OAuth 1.0a (signed requests, which fits OTHER, not OAuth2). Admin and customer tokens are issued in exchange for username and password; the bare integration token as a bearer is off by default. Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service uses Adobe IMS OAuth2 client credentials.
access_notes: Magento Open Source is free and self-hosted, so a developer can run a store and create an integration. Adobe Commerce cloud and on-prem need a merchant license or contract. There is no central sandbox, and each merchant creates credentials in their own admin.
blocker_notes: Every merchant runs their own instance, so a toolkit needs a per-customer base URL and integration credentials. OAuth 1.0a signing is non-standard for multi-user access.

evidence.quote: OAuth authentication with Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source is based on [OAuth 1.0a](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5849), an open standard for secure API authentication.
When you request a token from one of these services, the service returns a unique access token in exchange for an account's username and password.
Magento Open Source, the core with the same REST and GraphQL framework, is free under OSL 3.0, so an owner can start on a self-hosted store with no contract.
Adobe Commerce on Cloud, Adobe Commerce on-premises, and Magento Open Source all use the same REST API framework.
Turns every service method that a `webapi.xml` route calls into an *ability*, for example `catalog.product_repository.get_list`. A store has about 600 of them.
This is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that connects to a Magento Open Source or Adobe Commerce REST API making possible Claude, OpenAI Agent Builder and other MCP clients
